question: Does the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental trawl survey provide fish evidence that can be assigned to Manila Bay sectors without treating the bay-wide study as point-level or current occurrence data?

source.title: Species composition, distribution, biomass trends and exploitation of dominant fish species in Manila Bay using experimental trawl survey
source.citation: Bendaño, A. P., Lopez, G. D. V., Perez, M. A., Santos, M. D., & Torres, F. S. B. Jr. (2017). Species composition, distribution, biomass trends and exploitation of dominant fish species in Manila Bay using experimental trawl survey. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 24(1), 31–46. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/24.1.2016A0002

method.summary: Retrieved the official NFRDI-hosted publisher PDF and reviewed the abstract, study-area text, methods, Figure 3.1, results, and Table 3.2. Cross-checked title, authors, issue, pages, and DOI against the NFRDI journal article page and repository record.
accessNotes: The PDF reports a field trawl survey from March 2014 through October 2015 at 16 predetermined stations, with 156 tows in 3–46 m depths and ten fishing trips.
Figure 3.1 shows the 16 numbered dragging stations within Manila Bay and neighboring labels for Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Bataan, and Cavite.

Table 3.2 is a raster/scanned table whose caption describes the top 50 fish and invertebrate taxa by biomass abundance across five named sectors. Its legend groups commonness by the proportion of hauls and marks not-found entries.
The article gives no station coordinate table or row-level occurrence dataset in the reviewed material. The scanned table's taxa and sector symbols were not transcribed.
method.reuseFinding: The publisher PDF is accessible, but no article-specific license or item-level permission to redistribute its table, map, or underlying observations was verified. Retain attributed bibliographic metadata and a concise scope summary only.

sourceFindings.scope: The study abstract reports 146 fish and invertebrate species in 48 families across Manila Bay. Methods report 16 predetermined stations, 156 tows, depths of 3–46 m, and the March 2014–October 2015 survey interval.
sourceFindings.limits: These are historical survey-wide totals. They are not the number of fish taxa, a municipality-specific checklist, current presence, or a complete species inventory for any one sector.
sourceFindings.attribution: Use only as historical, gear-specific evidence of trawl catches in Manila Bay.

sourceFindings.scope: Table 3.2 groups its top 50 fish-and-invertebrate taxa under Cavite, Bulacan–Pampanga, Metro Manila, Bataan, and Corregidor Island. Its symbols express the proportion of hauls in which each listed taxon was common; the caption says the table covers taxa caught during the survey.
sourceFindings.limits: The sectors are broad labels and the table image has not been transcribed. The map does not expose digital haul coordinates. Sector aggregation cannot identify an individual city, estero, river, shoreline, municipal-water boundary, or station-level record.
sourceFindings.attribution: Retain the table as a source lead for a future rights-reviewed manual extraction; do not create individual species or occurrence rows from this screen.

sourceFindings.scope: The results text reports total fish-and-invertebrate species counts by sampled bay sector: 100 near Cavite, 93 in the Pampanga–Bulacan area, 80 near Metro Manila, 55 near Bataan, and 42 near Corregidor Island.
sourceFindings.limits: These totals may overlap across sectors and are not counts of unique fish species, independently verified taxa, current stocks, or municipality coverage.
sourceFindings.attribution: Preserve the source wording and broad sector scope; do not sum these totals or treat them as administrative inventories.

relatedSourceAssessment.identityCrosswalk: The study is linked to the shared Manila Bay waterbody identity used in the existing National Museum GBIF/OBIS crosswalk only for waterbody-level catalog organization. No dataset or specimen lineage between this trawl study and the National Museum collection is established.
relatedSourceAssessment.relatedLandingStudies: A separate Manila Bay landing-site assessment surfaced during discovery but was not used to validate this trawl study or counted as the same survey. Any future comparison must check sampling frames and cohort overlap before combining species or counts.

interpretation: The article documents historical trawl catches across Manila Bay, including a table organized into five broad bay sectors. This is a valuable research lead for the shared L1/L2/L3 marine-water evidence lane.

The sector labels are not official geographic boundaries. Keep Manila Bay represented once as a shared waterbody; do not allocate the Metro Manila sector to every NCR city or assign the Cavite sector to all Cavite municipal waters.
The top-50 table is a mixed fish-and-invertebrate summary. No taxon names or sector symbols were transcribed during this screen, and no species or occurrence assertions are added.
The 2014–2015 sampling period does not support current-presence, catchability, fishing advice, harvest legality, or safety claims.
No table, map, exact coordinates, raw survey data, public species row, geometry, or app projection is admitted.

decision.reason: The primary source provides historical sector-level catch evidence, but the scanned table was not transcribed, exact station coordinates are not provided, and reuse terms are unverified. Catalog it for subsequent taxon and rights review without creating regional species rows.

nextActions: Locate a higher-resolution or author-provided version of Table 3.2 and verify reuse terms before any manual species/sector extraction.

If a permitted extraction becomes available, separate fish from invertebrates, normalize names with a pinned taxonomic backbone, preserve the source's survey interval and sector labels, and do not treat dash entries as biological absence.
Crosswalk any extracted sector labels to a shared Manila Bay waterbody record while keeping L1, L2, and L3 administrative shoreline coverage distinct.
Continue independent freshwater, brackish, river, lake, wetland, and estero source discovery; this source covers marine trawl catches only.

sources.supports: Official NFRDI-hosted full article PDF, including the survey abstract, methods, study-area map, results, and sector-grouped Table 3.2.
NFRDI journal article landing page and publication metadata.
NFRDI repository metadata for the 2017 article and its downloadable PDF.
